meta.about: Founded in 2010, Brainbees Solutions Limited offers products for mothers, babies, and kids through its online platform 'FirstCry'.[1]

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments._why: India GMV grew 11% in FY26 (Q4 +12%) and 12% in Q1FY27, with revenue +17.7%. Management expects growth to stay "elevated" (RocketBees >50% of shipments, Qwik in 12 cities, ~100 new stores in FY27 after a pause). JM Financial assumes group GMV +13% / +12% / +12% (May-2026). We assume 13% a year: Q1's pace plus stores, below the high-teens of FY24.
segments._revWhy: Revenue was 58.8% of India GMV in FY26 and 61.1% in Q1FY27 (own manufacturing sales; GST cuts lowered MRP-based GMV). Held at 60.5%.
segments._marginWhy: Adjusted EBITDA was 8.8% of revenue in FY26 (9.5% in FY25) but 5.7% in Q1FY27 after a ~260bp gross-margin hit (diaper price war; rupee and crude in own manufacturing). Management expects input costs passed on by end-Q2 and diaper pricing to normalise over 4-6 quarters. We assume 7.6% / 8.6% / 9.2% of revenue (4.6% / 5.2% / 5.55% of GMV): FY27E below FY26, FY29E still below FY25.

segments.name: International (UAE, KSA)
segments._why: GMV +5% in FY26 (Q4 +2%) and +9% in Q1FY27 despite Gulf geopolitics and promotions by two horizontals. 9% / 11% / 12%.
segments._revWhy: Revenue was 50.9% of GMV in FY26 and 54.4% in Q1FY27 (more first-party sales); 53%.
segments._marginWhy: Adjusted EBITDA -9.6% of revenue in FY26, -7.2% in Q1FY27 (-25% in FY23). No breakeven date. We assume -6% / -3.5% / -1.5% of revenue (-3.2% / -1.85% / -0.8% of GMV): breakeven around FY30E.

assumptions._esopWhy: Share-based pay was ₹224 cr in FY26 and ₹30 cr in Q1FY27. The company's schedule for options already granted is ₹118 / 64 / 30 cr for FY27-FY29 (Q1FY27 presentation, slide 43); we add ~₹15-30 cr a year for new grants from FY28E.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex ₹189 cr in FY26 (₹186 cr PPE + intangibles) plus ~₹145 cr of new leases (right-of-use additions), which the engine must carry so depreciation keeps pace. ~100 new stores in FY27 and more in FY28: ₹350 / 400 / 430 cr incl. leases.

Q1FY27 ₹47 cr (Q1FY26 ₹48 cr). The fixed ₹175-180 cr plus the yield gives ₹184 cr in FY27E, in line with FY26 and the Q1 run-rate.

assumptions._interestWhy: Finance cost ₹156 cr in FY26 (lease interest ₹103 cr) and ₹37 cr in Q1FY27; rising with new store leases.

cover.headline: A leader that lost its growth, priced as if it will not get it back
cover.lead: FirstCry (Brainbees Solutions) is India's largest specialist retailer of baby and kids' products: ₹11,644 cr of orders in FY26 through its app and 1,188 stores, plus a loss-making Gulf business and 51.68% of Globalbees, a D2C brand roll-up. India growth has re-accelerated (revenue +17.7% in Q1FY27), but a diaper price war with quick-commerce apps cut the India margin to 5.7% and the group still lost ₹31 cr in the quarter. The stock trades at ₹{{P.last|num}}, 61% below its ₹465 IPO price and 0.97x next year's sales, against a 12-month median of 1.31x. Our sum of the parts at 1.15x Sep-28E sales gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with BUY.** Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}} ({{scen.bear.upside|chg}}). The street's consensus target is ₹243.

arguments.h: India is re-accelerating on fixes FirstCry controls
arguments.p: India multi-channel revenue grew 17.7% in Q1FY27, up every quarter from 7.5% a year earlier, as its own delivery network (RocketBees, >50% of online shipments), 2-3 hour FirstCry Qwik and re-assorted stores (offline GMV +15%) took hold; ~100 new stores are planned for FY27. The specialist assortment, home brands (>58% of India GMV) and 1,188 stores are hard to copy.

arguments.h: But margins went the wrong way, and the loss persists
arguments.p: A diaper price war with quick-commerce apps and higher input costs cut India gross margin ~260bp; India adjusted EBITDA fell to 5.7% of revenue (8.6% a year earlier). The group still lost ₹31 cr in Q1FY27. Adjusted EBITDA flatters: it excludes ESOP cost (₹224 cr in FY26) and rent (₹255 cr).

arguments.h: Half of Globalbees belongs to others
arguments.p: Minorities own 48.32% of Globalbees and FirstCry owes ₹388 cr of earn-outs to its brand founders. JM Financial values Globalbees at 100% (₹52/share); at FirstCry's share it is worth ~₹27. We deduct both.

arguments.h: Valuation: below 1x sales, the stock has de-rated too far
arguments.p: At ₹180 (61% below the ₹465 IPO price) the market pays 0.97x next year's attributable sales, against a 12-month median of 1.31x, while internet peers de-rated −11.8%. At our derived 1.15x Sep-28E sales the sum of the parts gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): BUY. The street's consensus target is ₹243.

sections.title: A specialist for parents, online and in stores, with three side businesses

blocks.p: FirstCry sells everything a family needs from pregnancy to a child's twelfth year: diapers, baby care, clothes, footwear, toys, strollers, nursery and school supplies. Parents buy through its app and website (78% of India GMV) or 1,188 FirstCry and BabyHug stores, most run by franchisees. More than half of what it sells in India is its own brands (BabyHug and others), some made in its own plants; the rest comes from 7,900+ brands. A parenting app and partnerships with 13,500+ hospitals bring in new parents. Around this core sit three other segments: **International** (online in the UAE and Saudi Arabia), **Globalbees** (51.68% of a group of D2C brands sold mostly on marketplaces) and **Others** (preschools).

sections.title: Sixteen years to build India's baby-products leader; a roll-up and an IPO along the way

blocks.p: FirstCry started in Pune in 2010 as an online shop for baby products. It added stores (company-owned and franchised), its own BabyHug and other home brands, a parenting app and community, and its own manufacturing. It took the model to the UAE (2019) and Saudi Arabia (2022) and built Globalbees, a roll-up of direct-to-consumer brands, in FY22-FY23. Venture investors, led by SoftBank, and Mahindra & Mahindra funded years of losses; the IPO in Aug-2024 raised ₹1,666 cr of new money and let early holders sell ₹2,528 cr of shares. There is no promoter: the company is "professionally managed" and the founder holds 5.2%.

sections.title: A large, fast-growing market where quick commerce now fights for the daily basket

blocks.p: India's childcare market is projected by RedSeer (July-2024 report, cited in the FY26 annual report) to grow 12-14% a year; childcare products alone are put at ₹5,150-5,450 bn by FY29 in India, against ₹640-680 bn in Saudi Arabia and ₹240-280 bn in the UAE. Spending per child is far lower in India (₹9,280-9,350 in FY24) than in KSA (₹61,000-71,000) or the UAE (₹160,000-170,000). About 21% of India's population is aged 0-12.

Diapers (~15% of India GMV) became a price war from Q3FY26 as quick-commerce apps and horizontals with fresh capital used them to win young parents; pharmacy chains launched own-label diapers. In the Gulf, two horizontal e-commerce players that entered in 2024 kept promotions high. GST rationalisation (from Q2FY26) moved most childcare products to the 5% slab: good for organised retail, but it lowered MRPs, so GMV (measured at MRP) grew slower than revenue in Q1FY27.

sections.title: India multi-channel: growth is back; the gross margin is not yet

blocks.p: India multi-channel is FirstCry: the app and website (78% of GMV) and 1,188 stores (22%), selling 2.1 mn products from 7,900+ brands, with its own BabyHug and other home brands at more than half of GMV. It made ₹505 cr of adjusted EBITDA in FY26 (8.8% of revenue) and is profitable after tax. Growth slowed to 7.5-9% in the first three quarters of FY26 as third-party couriers let customers down, stores carried too wide a range and quick-commerce apps cut diaper prices. The company built its own delivery network (RocketBees, 72 cities, >50% of shipments), a 2-3 hour service (FirstCry Qwik, 12 cities) and re-assorted its stores toward fewer, cheaper lines. Revenue growth recovered to 17.7% in Q1FY27. But gross margin fell ~280bp YoY in Q4FY26 and ~260bp in Q1FY27, and adjusted EBITDA dropped to 5.7% of revenue.

sections.title: International: a big prize in the Gulf, still losing money after six years

blocks.p: FirstCry sells online in the UAE (since 2019) and Saudi Arabia (since 2022), where parents spend 7-18 times more per child than in India and average orders are 4.1x India's. Revenue was ₹947 cr in FY26 (+10%) and ₹232 cr in Q1FY27 (+12%). Two horizontal players entered in 2024 and kept promotions high, so GMV grew only 5% in FY26. FirstCry chose margin over growth: gross margin rose to 27.7% in Q1FY27 and the adjusted EBITDA loss fell from ₹140 cr in FY25 to ₹91 cr in FY26 (−7% of revenue in Q1FY27, −25% in FY23). blocks.p: Globalbees bought stakes in D2C brands (home improvement, appliances, health and personal care, lifestyle) in FY22-FY23 and has grown organically since its last deal in Sep-2022. Revenue was ₹1,894 cr in FY26 (+20%; core brands +28%) and flat in Q1FY27 (a planned warehouse move at one core brand and a change in Flipkart's settlement model). sections.title: Reported vs adjusted: ESOPs, rent, brand amortisation and recurring "one-offs"

blocks.p: FirstCry's headline measure, **adjusted EBITDA** (₹486 cr in FY26, 5.7% of revenue), leaves out four real costs. ESOP cost (₹224 cr) is a genuine expense paid in shares. Rent (₹255 cr of lease payments) sits in depreciation and interest under Ind AS 116. Brand amortisation (₹88 cr) reflects the price paid for Globalbees brands. Exceptional items (₹50 cr: impairments, write-offs, a fire) have appeared every year. After depreciation on equipment, interest, tax (₹37 cr paid by profitable entities while others lose money) and minorities (₹63 cr), the loss attributable to shareholders was ₹140 cr. The company's own "cash profit after tax" (₹312 cr) adds back ESOP, amortisation and exceptionals but deducts cash rent.

bullets: **Exceptional items are not exceptional.** ₹50 cr in FY25, ₹50 cr in FY26 and ₹18 cr in Q1FY27, mostly Globalbees impairments and inventory write-offs. FY25 hid a ₹197 cr impairment behind a ₹174 cr gain from cutting the earn-outs owed to brand founders.

**Two "EBITDA"s.** Screener's EBITDA (₹262 cr in FY26) is after ESOP cost; the company's adjusted EBITDA (₹486 cr) is before it. Our model and Excel follow Screener for history and deduct ESOP in forecasts.

**Minorities.** Screener's headline net profit is before minorities; we use profit attributable to owners for history. Our forecast EPS includes 100% of Globalbees profit (the engine has no minority line); JM Financial (May-2026) expects minorities to take ₹53 cr in FY28E and ₹112 cr in FY29E, so our forecast EPS overstates what reaches FirstCry's shareholders.
**Tax is paid in a loss year**, because profits in India multi-channel cannot be set off against losses elsewhere; our FY27E assumes ~₹42 cr.
**Earn-outs:** ₹388 cr owed to Globalbees brand founders sits in other financial liabilities; changes in its value go through exceptional items.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Disclosure is good (segment P&Ls, reconciliations, an ESOP schedule, cash profit), the auditor (Walker Chandiok) gave a clean opinion, and the IPO-proceeds monitoring is published. But adjusted EBITDA excludes ESOP and rent, "exceptional" charges recur, and earn-out remeasurements can flatter profit.

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest specialist in baby and kids' products, online and in 1,188 stores, with its own brands at more than half of sales, growth re-accelerating (India revenue +17.7% in Q1FY27), net cash and no need for new equity. Plus a loss-making Gulf business, half of a D2C brand roll-up and a small, profitable preschool chain. Our sum of the parts gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).

**What you are paying for:** ~₹9,580 cr of market value, ~0.91x our Sep-28E attributable sales (₹10,617 cr), below the stock's own 12-month median (1.31x) and our 1.15x, after internet stocks de-rated −11.8%. If it does (input costs passed on, the diaper war cools), the stock is cheap; if quick commerce keeps diapers as a permanent loss-leader, our bear case (~flat) is the outcome. The company still reports a loss, and the DCF (₹{{dcf.blend.methods.1.value|num}}) does not support the price on today's margins.

assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex ₹189 cr in FY26 (₹186 cr PPE + intangibles) plus ~₹145 cr of new leases (right-of-use additions), which the engine must carry so depreciation keeps pace. ~100 new stores in FY27 and more in FY28: ₹350 / 400 / 430 cr incl. leases.

primary.name: Sum of the parts
primary.why: The street's method (JM Financial: segment SOTP on FY28E). Each segment at the EV/sales multiple derived from FirstCry's own trading and the sector move, Globalbees minorities and earn-outs deducted, plus net cash. Primary.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: India GMV grows ~16% a year as Qwik and new stores work and the diaper war ends; gross margin fully recovers (India adjusted EBITDA ~10% of revenue by FY29E); Globalbees grows ~20% at 7-8%; International breaks even by FY29E. Valued at FirstCry's own 12-month median EV/sales with no sector discount.
